checks.rule: OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.008 m in plan.
OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.020 m in height.
OSTN15 defines OSGB36 National Grid in conjunction with OS Net stations.
OSTN15 transformation error can be considered negligible relative to GNSS position error for the stated framework.
Agreement between OSTN15 and old triangulation network stations is about 0.1 m RMS for Great Britain.
OSGM15 Great Britain vertical-datum standard error is 0.008 m excluding GNSS heighting error.
Keep GNSS positioning error separate from OSTN15 transformation-model error in the parcel uncertainty budget.
Keep GNSS heighting error separate from OSGM15 vertical-datum model error.
Do not compare WGS84/GNSS coordinates directly with OSGB36 parcel geometry without an explicit valid transformation.
Do not report centimetre-level parcel precision merely because OS Net station coordinates have centimetre-level standard errors.
Record horizontal and vertical reference systems independently for every measured candidate.
A transformed elevation sample is accepted only when the coordinate and vertical-datum provenance are both known.
